replies.body: Added a failure-path test. `AbstractEmbeddingsTest.connectionError` (connects to a dead port, so no external service needed) is now mode-aware: under `emitExceptionAsLogs()` it asserts a `gen_ai.client.operation.exception` log record with `Severity.WARN` and the exception attributes, and otherwise asserts the span exception event. This runs via a new per-module `testExceptionSignalLogs` Gradle task (library + javaagent). The new `testExceptionSignalLogs` task does not set `testLatestDeps`, but `AbstractOpenAiTest` selects its helper based on `TestLatestDeps.testLatestDeps()`, which is driven by the `testLatestDeps` *system property* (cached at class init). As a result, when running with `-PtestLatestDeps=true`, the normal `test` task and this new task can execute the same tests against different helpers/expectations.

Set the same `testLatestDeps` system property on this task to keep behavior consistent with the main `test` task.

replies.body: Fixed. The OpenAI library now applies `systemProperty("testLatestDeps", otelProps.testLatestDeps)` via `withType<Test>().configureEach`, so both the default `test` task and `testExceptionSignalLogs` use the same helper selection path from `AbstractOpenAiTest`.

threads.body:
The new `testExceptionSignalLogs` task doesn’t inherit the system properties configured on the main `test` task (`testLatestDeps` and `collectMetadata`). `testLatestDeps` is used (and cached) by `TestLatestDeps.testLatestDeps()` in the OpenAI test base, so running with `-PtestLatestDeps=true` can make this task execute with different helper/expectations than the normal tests; and `collectMetadata` should match the rest of the javaagent test runs.

Mirror the relevant system properties from the `test` task here.

replies.body: Good catch. Mirrored the relevant system properties onto both `testExceptionSignalLogs` tasks: the javaagent task now sets `testLatestDeps` and `collectMetadata` (plus `metadataConfig=otel.semconv.exception.signal.preview=logs`, matching the other preview/semconv tasks), and the library task sets `testLatestDeps`. `testLatestDeps` is justified here since `AbstractOpenAiTest` reads it via `TestLatestDeps.testLatestDeps()` to select the test helper.

Follow-up: I refined this to configure the shared properties via `withType<Test>().configureEach` instead of duplicating them in `test` and `testExceptionSignalLogs`. The javaagent module now applies `testLatestDeps`, `collectMetadata`, and message capture to all Test tasks; the library module applies `testLatestDeps` to all Test tasks. `metadataConfig=otel.semconv.exception.signal.preview=logs` remains only on the preview-mode task.

[Testing] In `connectionError`, the span assertion only checks `hasException(thrown)` when span-events mode is enabled, but it doesn’t assert the *absence* of an exception event when running in `otel.semconv.exception.signal.preview=logs` (logs-only) mode. That means a regression that double-emits (span event + log) would still pass this test.

You can make this mode-aware assertion stricter by always calling `hasException(...)` with a conditional value (as done in `InstrumenterTest`).

[Testing] This test is effectively a no-op under the default build: `SemconvExceptionSignal.emitExceptionAsLogs()` is computed once at class init from the JVM’s `-Dotel.semconv.exception.signal.preview` (or declarative config). Since this module’s tests aren’t launched with that flag, the test will usually take the `else` branch and never validate the extractor behavior.

To make this test actually cover the preview behavior, set the system property to `logs` *before* the instrumenter is used (so `SemconvExceptionSignal` is initialized with the right value), and then assert the emitted log record. If `emitExceptionAsLogs()` is still false, fail fast (it indicates the flag was not applied early enough / requires a separate JVM test task).
